title: BA Documentation
summary: Turn Business Needs into Traceable Delivery Artifacts.
overview: BA documentation is a connected artifact ecosystem: each deliverable should make a business decision, requirement, design choice, or test outcome traceable to the next.
Different delivery models need different documentation depth. Use only the artifacts that add clarity, control, and evidence; avoid duplicate sources of truth.
Business Need → Business Requirement → Process and Rules → Functional Requirement → Design → User Story → API/Data Specification → Testing → Release → Traceability.

phases.title: Discovery & Initiation
phases.purpose: Define the business problem, scope, stakeholders, and current-state evidence.

phases.title: Business Analysis & Requirements
phases.purpose: Turn needs into testable business and functional requirements.

phases.title: Functional / Solution Design
phases.purpose: Describe expected user and system behaviour without replacing engineering design.

phases.title: Agile Delivery
phases.purpose: Make delivery slices clear and independently verifiable.

phases.title: UX & Process Modelling
phases.purpose: Show actors, decisions, handoffs, rework, and exceptions.

phases.title: Integration & Data
phases.purpose: Define business meaning across interfaces and systems of record.

phases.title: Testing & UAT
phases.purpose: Demonstrate that agreed requirements work in realistic business scenarios.

phases.title: Release & Change
phases.purpose: Assess readiness, impact, dependencies, and operational change.

phases.title: Governance & Traceability
phases.purpose: Maintain decision, approval, risk, and change evidence.

artifacts.title: BRD — Business Requirements Document
artifacts.summary: Defines the business need, scope, requirements, controls, and success measures. Exact structures vary by organisation.
learn: Use when stakeholders need an agreed business baseline before solution detail.
Do not use as a substitute for detailed system behaviour or an Agile backlog.
sample: Internal Fund Transfer: customers need to move funds between eligible accounts subject to applicable policy and configured controls.

artifacts.title: SRS — Software Requirements Specification
artifacts.summary: Describes expected system behaviour. BRD explains business need; SRS explains solution behaviour.
learn: Use for roles, functional behaviour, validations, UI, integration, data, errors, security, audit, and NFRs.
Do not assume every organisation uses the BRD/SRS names in the same way.
sample: Transfer submission validates eligible accounts and returns a business outcome or actionable error.
template: UI, API, data, error, security and audit requirements

artifacts.title: User Story + Acceptance Criteria
artifacts.summary: A delivery-sized expression of user value with observable acceptance conditions.
learn: Cover happy path, validation, permissions, exceptions, state changes, and auditability where applicable.
sample: As a banking customer, I want to transfer funds to another eligible account, so that I can move money securely.
Given eligible details, when I confirm, then the service records the transfer outcome.
template: Linked rule, requirement, design, and test IDs

artifacts.title: Requirement Traceability Matrix
artifacts.summary: Connects requirements to design, delivery, tests, and release evidence.
learn: Use for change impact, coverage checks, and release readiness.

artifacts.title: Business Rules Catalogue
artifacts.summary: A governed catalogue of business decisions distinct from UI validation.
learn: State trigger, condition, outcome, source, and owner; keep policy values configurable where unknown.
sample: An account is eligible only when it satisfies applicable product and authorisation policy.

artifacts.title: Figma / Screen Specification
artifacts.summary: Explains functional screen behaviour; Figma is not itself a complete functional specification.
learn: Specify fields, source, validation, visibility, states, actions, and transitions.
sample: Source Account, Beneficiary Account, Amount, Currency, Transfer Date, Reference, Continue, Confirm.
template: Validation, error, business rule, visibility, state

artifacts.title: Draw.io Process Flow
artifacts.summary: A simple business flow shows activities and decisions without BPMN notation overhead.
learn: Use early to align on happy path, exceptions, handoffs, and rework.
sample: Customer initiates transfer → digital banking validates → required control checks → processing → core posting → notification.

artifacts.title: BPMN / Swimlane Process
artifacts.summary: Swimlanes clarify ownership; BPMN adds formal events, gateways, and flows. Neither is a sequence diagram.
learn: Use where cross-team control, approval, and exception accountability need precision.
sample: Customer, Digital Banking, Risk/Control, Approval, Payment Processing, Core Banking, Notification lanes.

artifacts.title: API Requirement / API Mapping
artifacts.summary: Captures business interface needs, not a vendor-specific Swagger contract.
learn: Define purpose, trigger, consumer, provider, preconditions, business fields, outcomes, errors, dependencies, and trace IDs.
sample: Transfer request uses source account, beneficiary account, amount, currency, date, and reference according to supported product configuration.

artifacts.title: Data Dictionary / Field Mapping
artifacts.summary: Defines data meaning and ownership; a data dictionary is not the same as source-to-target mapping.
learn: Identify system of record, derived values, validation, transformation, owner, and traceability.
sample: Transfer Reference: customer-provided business reference, stored subject to applicable data rules.

artifacts.title: UAT Test Cases
artifacts.summary: Turns accepted requirements into executable business verification and evidence.
learn: Acceptance criteria guide tests but are not themselves the full UAT test case.
sample: UAT-IFT-025 verifies a permitted customer can submit eligible transfer details and receive the expected outcome.

artifacts.title: Impact Assessment
artifacts.summary: Assesses change across customer, operations, process, systems, integration, data, controls, reporting, support, release, and dependencies.
learn: Use before release planning; it is not the same as a change request.
sample: Internal Fund Transfer impact includes customer messaging, operational exceptions, downstream notifications, support readiness, and applicable controls.

bankingExample.title: Internal Fund Transfer
steps: Business problem: customers need a clear, controlled way to move funds between eligible accounts.
BRD records scope, stakeholders, requirements, rules, exceptions, and success criteria.
Process and BPMN show validation, required controls, approval where applicable, posting, exception, and notification paths.
SRS, screen specification, stories, API/data mappings, and UAT cases refine the same requirement without creating a second source of truth.
RTM proves coverage through release and governance evidence.
